arxiv-1705-10544.title: On the TASEP with Second Class Particles
arxiv-1705-10544.creator: Eunghyun LEE
arxiv-1705-10544.description: Abstract In this paper we study some conditional probabilities for the totally asymmetric simple exclusion processes (TASEP) with second class particles. To be more specific, we consider a finite system with one first class particle and N − 1 N-1 second class particles, and we assume that the first class particle is initially at the leftmost position.

arxiv-2106-00501.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Qihui Wu, Tianchen Ruan, Fuhui Zhou, Yang Huang, Fan Xu, Shijin Zhao, Ya Liu, and Xuyang Huang. Many machine learning frameworks have been proposed and used in wireless communications for realizing diverse goals. However, their incapability of adapting to the dynamic wireless environment and tasks and of self-learning limit their extensive applications and achievable performance.

arxiv-2111-08167.creator: Yan-Fei Li, Yue-Yue Chen, Karen Z. Hatsagortsyan, Christoph H. Keitel
arxiv-2111-08167.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yan-Fei Li, Yue-Yue Chen, Karen Z. Hatsagortsyan, Christoph H. Keitel. Electron beam longitudinal polarization during the interaction with counterpropagating circularly-polarized ultraintense laser pulses is investigated, while accounting for the anomalous magnetic moment of the electron.

arxiv-2205-00196.title: Effects of the acceleration on holographic complexity
arxiv-2205-00196.creator: Koichi Nagasaki
arxiv-2205-00196.description: Abstract In this work we consider a spacial kind of spacetime called AdS accelerating black holes. This is a kind of black holes which have a stringlike singularity along polar axises attached to the black hole and it accelerates the black hole.

arxiv-2301-01600.title: 5G on the Farm: Evaluating Wireless Network Capabilities for Agricultural Robotics
arxiv-2301-01600.creator: Tsvetan Zhivkov, Elizabeth I Sklar
arxiv-2301-01600.description: Abstract Global food security is an issue that is fast becoming a critical matter in the world today. Global warming, climate change and a range of other impacts caused by humans, such as carbon emissions, sociopolitical and economical challenges (e.g. war), traditional workforce/labour decline and population growth are straining global food security.

arxiv-2303-08234.title: Dynamics of dissipative Landau-Zener transitions in an anisotropic three-level system
arxiv-2303-08234.creator: Lixing Zhang 1 , Lu Wang 2 , Maxim F. Gelin 3 and Yang Zhao 1
arxiv-2303-08234.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Lixing Zhang 1 , Lu Wang 2 , Maxim F. Gelin 3 and Yang Zhao 1. We investigate the dynamics of Landau-Zener (LZ) transitions in an anisotropic, dissipative three-level LZ model (3-LZM) using the numerically accurate multiple Davydov D 2 \mathrm{D}_{2} Ansatz in the framework of the time-dependent variational principle. It is demonstrated that a non-monotonic relationship exists between the Landau-Zener transition probability and the phonon coupling strength when the 3-LZM is driven by a linear external field.

arxiv-2310-11337.title: On the Northcott property for infinite extensions
arxiv-2310-11337.creator: Martin Widmer
arxiv-2310-11337.description: Abstract . We start with a brief survey on the Northcott property for subfields of the algebraic numbers ℚ ¯ \overline{\mathbb{\mathchar 29009}} . Then we introduce a new criterion for its validity (refining the author’s previous criterion), addressing a problem of Bombieri.

arxiv-2403-14997.creator: Bhargav Jha and Shaunak D. Bopardikar, Alexander Von Moll, David Casbeer
arxiv-2403-14997.description: Abstract 1 Introduction A ship with a firing turret, mobile air-defense system, surveillance aircraft, and military vehicles with directed sensors are all examples of moving pursuers with rotating platforms installed onboard. The rotating platforms can be a turret, a missile launcher, or a gimballed camera or sensor.

arxiv-2406-05121.title: Energy Propagation in Scattering Convolution Networks Can Be Arbitrarily Slow
arxiv-2406-05121.creator: Hartmut Führ, Max Getter
arxiv-2406-05121.description: Abstract . We analyze energy decay for deep convolutional neural networks employed as feature extractors, such as Mallat’s wavelet scattering transform. For time-frequency scattering transforms based on Gabor filters, it has been established that energy decay is exponential, for arbitrary square-integrable input signals. Our main results allow to prove that this is wrong for wavelet scattering in arbitrary dimensions.

arxiv-2407-19561.title: Anti-Concentration for the Unitary Haar Measure and Applications to Random Quantum Circuits
arxiv-2407-19561.creator: Bill Fefferman, Soumik Ghosh, Wei Zhan
arxiv-2407-19561.description: Abstract We prove a Carbery-Wright style anti-concentration inequality for the unitary Haar measure, by showing that the probability of a polynomial in the entries of a random unitary falling into an ε \varepsilon range is at most a polynomial in ε \varepsilon .

arxiv-2503-06252.title: Can Atomic Step Decomposition Enhance the Self-structured Reasoning of Multimodal Large Models?
arxiv-2503-06252.creator: Kun Xiang, Zhili Liu, Zihao Jiang, Yunshuang Nie, Kaixin Cai, Yiyang Yin, Runhui Huang, Haoxiang Fan, Hanhui Li, Weiran Huang, Yihan Zeng, Yu-Jie Yuan, Jianhua Han, Lanqing Hong, Hang Xu, Xiaodan Liang
arxiv-2503-06252.description: Abstract In this paper, we address the challenging task of multimodal mathematical reasoning by incorporating the ability of ”slow thinking” into multimodal large language models (MLLMs). Our core idea is that different levels of reasoning abilities can be combined dynamically to tackle questions with different complexity.

arxiv-2510-15731.title: Attention Sinks in Diffusion Language Models
arxiv-2510-15731.creator: Maximo Eduardo Rulli Simone Petruzzi Edoardo Michielon, Fabrizio Silvestri Simone Scardapane Alessio Devoto
arxiv-2510-15731.description: Abstract Masked Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) have recently emerged as a promising alternative to traditional Autoregressive Models (ARMs). DLMs employ transformer encoders with bidirectional attention, enabling parallel token generation while maintaining competitive performance. Although their efficiency and effectiveness have been extensively studied, the internal mechanisms that govern DLMs remain largely unexplored.

pmc-11385619.title: Contribution of kelp dashi liquid to sustainable maintenance of taste sensation and promotion of healthy eating in older adults throughout the umami-taste salivary reflex
pmc-11385619.creator: Shizuko Satoh-Kuriwada, Satoshi Gotoh, Noriaki Shoji, Hisayuki Uneyama, Michio Komai
pmc-11385619.description: IntroductionTaste decline, including taste loss in older adults, leads to malnutrition and frailty. In a super-aging society, improving taste decline and maintaining taste sensation are crucial for the wellbeing of older adults. Hyposalivation frequently affects older individuals and is the leading cause of taste decline in older adults.

pmc-11463265.title: Advantages and Disadvantages of Reconstructive and Preservation Rhinoplasty: Surgical Techniques, Outcomes, and Future Directions
pmc-11463265.creator: Christopher R Meretsky, Andreas Polychronis, David Clark, Dimitria Liovas, Anthony T Schiuma
pmc-11463265.description: Reconstructive rhinoplasty, a specialized surgical procedure, aims to restore both the form and function of the nose, particularly after trauma, congenital defects, or prior surgeries. This review evaluates the advantages and disadvantages of various surgical techniques used in reconstructive and preservation rhinoplasty.

pmc-12447387.title: Redox-Driven Exsolution and Dissolution Behavior of High-Entropy Spinel Catalysts: A Comparative Study of MnFeCoNiCuO x and MnCoNiCuZnO x
pmc-12447387.creator: Pei-Tung Chou, Cheng-Chia Kuo, Po-Yang Peng, Ying-Rui Lu, Chi-Liang Chen, Yu-Chuan Lin
pmc-12447387.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). High-entropy oxides (HEOs) offer tunable redox chemistry and thermal stability for catalytic applications. Here, we compare two spinel-type HEOs, MnFeCoNiCuO x and MnCoNiCuZnO x , with similar configurational entropy but different redox behaviors under reverse water–gas shift (RWGS) conditions. Only MnFeCoNiCuO x exhibits reversible exsolution and reincorporation of Fe/Co/Ni/Cu alloy nanoparticles (NPs) during H2–CO2 cycling, as confirmed by in situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy and wavelet-transformation.

pmc-13254292.title: Insects manipulate host nuclear trafficking and epigenetic regulation to facilitate herbivory
pmc-13254292.creator: Ze-Long Zhang, Tang-Bin Hu, Xin-Ye Xu, Hai-Bin Lu, Jia-Bao Lu, Ji-Chong Zhuo, Yi-Zhe Wang, Zong-Tao Sun, Jian-Ping Chen, Jun-Min Li, Chuan-Xi Zhang, Hai-Jian Huang
pmc-13254292.description: Effectors secreted by pathogens or insects manipulate host plant cellular processes depending on their target destination. However, our current knowledge regarding nucleus-localized effectors from herbivorous insects remains limited. Here, we demonstrate that Nilaparvata lugens evolve a nuclear localization signal (NLS)-containing salivary effector NlAMSP that is specialized for targeting host plants.

pmc-13326791.title: First‐Line Treatment of IGHV‐Unmutated Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia: A Network Meta‐Analysis of Targeted and Chemoimmunotherapy Regimens
pmc-13326791.creator: Santino Caserta, Enrica Antonia Martino, Danilo Lofaro, Ernesto Vigna, Antonella Bruzzese, Francesco Mendicino, Maria Eugenia Alvaro, Caterina Labanca, Eugenio Lucia, Virginia Olivito, Nicola Amodio, Fortunato Morabito, Valter Gattei, Massimo Gentile
pmc-13326791.description: Immunoglobulin heavy chain variable region‐unmutated (IGHV‐U) chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) represents a biologically aggressive subgroup with limited responsiveness to chemoimmunotherapy (CIT). To clarify the comparative effectiveness of available frontline options, we conducted a comprehensive Bayesian network meta‐analysis of randomized clinical trials including more than 4500 IGHV‐U patients.

pmc-13336109.title: Prior Expectations Bias Confidence Judgments Through Parietal Alpha‐Band Modulation
pmc-13336109.creator: Luca Tarasi, Anna Pasini, Domenico Romanazzi, Margherita Covelli, Vincenzo Romei
pmc-13336109.description: Humans possess the metacognitive ability to estimate the likely accuracy of their own decisions through confidence judgments. Yet, whether prior information shapes confidence and the neural mechanisms mediating such influence, remain to be determined. Here, two complementary studies identify parietal alpha modulation as an oscillatory mechanism linking prior expectations to selective shifts in metacognitive bias.

pmc-13341248.title: “Nerves Need Nourishment”: Advertising Phospho-Energon Pills in Early Twentieth-Century Sweden
pmc-13341248.creator: Lauren Alex O’Hagan, Leif Runefelt
pmc-13341248.description: This paper offers the first case study of Phospho-Energon — an early twentieth-century Swedish patent medicine believed to cure nervousness. Using a large dataset of newspaper advertisements, it explores how the product was presented through scientific and medical language, which drew upon a range of visual and verbal rhetoric to convince consumers of its benefits.

uslaw-usc-t36-s144.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t36-s144.description: United States Code, Title 36 (Patriotic And National Observances, Ceremonies, And Organizations); Part A (Observances And Ceremonies); Chapter 1 (Patriotic And National Observances). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Designation.— September 11 is Patriot Day.
